hr-5dX0.title: Coverage: autumn colours (older camera)
hr-5dX0.summary: Most older Gen 3 coverage was shot in autumn, so plants often look yellow or orange. The newer Gen 4 coverage does not have this.

hr-79X3.title: Sign: street names in two languages (Italian too)
hr-79X3.summary: Street name signs show both the local language and Italian, mostly in the western towns of the northern peninsula.

hr-7sgJ.title: Landmark: medieval city walls by the sea
hr-7sgJ.summary: Well-preserved medieval city walls visible from many spots in and around the old town, in the far south of the coast.

hr-9d6r.title: Landscape: hilly farmland north and west of the capital
hr-9d6r.summary: North and west of the capital the land is hilly and agricultural.

hr-AwCI.title: Landscape: many vineyards near the Serbian border
hr-AwCI.summary: Lots of vineyards in the far north-east near the Serbian border, west of Novi Sad. Vineyards exist elsewhere, but if you see many in the north-east, you are most likely here.

hr-ELIq.title: Landscape: rocky coastal mountains, shrubs, islands
hr-ELIq.summary: The Adriatic coast has rocky mountains like Montenegro or Albania, with shrubs more than trees, especially in the south, and many islands and peninsulas.

hr-FJLL.title: Pole: round concrete or wood, alternating hooks
hr-FJLL.summary: Round concrete or wooden poles, with wooden ones often having hooks alternating on each side. Somewhat like Latvian poles.

hr-FWfo.title: Coverage: old backpack camera in historic towns
hr-FWfo.summary: No older Gen 2 car coverage, but some historic town centres were shot with an old Gen 2 walking backpack. Sometimes the photographer's red cap is visible.

hr-KLL9.title: Google car: white car, never an antenna
hr-KLL9.summary: A white newer Gen 4 car that never has an antenna. Other European white cars usually show an antenna.

hr-KPaC.title: Language: town names ending in -ec
hr-KPaC.summary: Town names ending in -ec are common in the north of the central part of the country.

hr-M3t0.title: Language: Latin letters, IJE spellings
hr-M3t0.summary: A Slavic language always written in Latin letters. It often uses IJE where Serbian uses just E. Serbian and Montenegrin are very similar but may use Cyrillic.

differs.how: Serbian uses E instead of IJE and also Cyrillic
Montenegrin is similar but also uses Cyrillic

hr-MZYL.title: Google car: black car, never an antenna
hr-MZYL.summary: A black newer Gen 4 car that never has an antenna. Many European countries have black cars, but those usually show an antenna.

hr-O1bS.title: Coverage: big city, apartment blocks, blue trams
hr-O1bS.summary: A big-city feel with apartment blocks everywhere, hills in the north, and blue electric trams. Also has city walking-backpack coverage, often with the old Gen 2 camera.

hr-OmRw.title: Plate: long white, blue strip optional
hr-OmRw.summary: Long white plates, with or without a blue EU strip on the left. Older Gen 3 cars mostly have none; newer Gen 4 cars more often do. Strips are more common on the coast because of tourists.

hr-R9QL.title: Fire hydrant: blue with two diagonal arms
hr-R9QL.summary: Blue fire hydrants with two diagonal protrusions on the sides. Newer ones have a smaller top but are still blue. Neighbouring countries have similar ones, most often Hungary.

hr-asMp.title: Bollard: white, black rectangle, sharp triangle top
hr-asMp.summary: White post with a black rectangle and a red or white reflector. Seen from above it is a sharp-edged triangle. North Macedonia sometimes uses similar ones.

differs.how: Lithuanian ones are rounder with an orange reflector

hr-cTVj.title: Houses: ruined, being rebuilt
hr-cTVj.summary: Many ruined buildings undergoing repair, from a 2020 earthquake that heavily damaged the town.

hr-eUrn.title: Chevron: red arrow on yellow or white
hr-eUrn.summary: Curve chevrons show a red arrow on a yellow or white background.

hr-ffan.title: Pole: long blue traffic light arms
hr-ffan.summary: Traffic lights hang from long blue poles reaching over the road. They are only found in one coastal city.

hr-fguV.title: Landscape: red soil in the north-west peninsula
hr-fguV.summary: The north-western peninsula south of Trieste sometimes has clearly red soil.

hr-hHNn.title: Houses: beige brick, green shutters
hr-hHNn.summary: Houses and walls of beige brick, often with green shutters (sometimes white or beige) are common on the coast. Parts of Italy look similar.

hr-hPMC.title: Plants: tall cypress trees
hr-hPMC.summary: Tall cypress trees are common near the southern tip of the country.

hr-iF5g.title: Landscape: flat farmland in the north-east
hr-iF5g.summary: In the north-east the land is mostly flat with lots of farming. It looks like Hungary and north-west Serbia.

hr-kv7I.title: Landscape: flat with a mountain ridge to the north
hr-kv7I.summary: A flat area with a mountain ridge visible in the distance to the north. It lies north-east of the coastal city of Zadar.

hr-lm-2988.title: Sign: pedestrian with white belt, straight legs
hr-lm-2988.summary: The pedestrian figure has a white belt, non-pointed shoes and straight legs. The same figure is used in Bosnia; the belt also appears in Portugal, Germany and Hungary.

differs.how: Portugal also has a belt and non-pointed shoes
Germany also has a white belt
Hungary also has a white belt

hr-lm-395595.title: Phone numbers: landline area codes
hr-lm-395595.summary: Landlines start with a zero then the area code: 01 for the capital, 02X in the south, 05X north-west, 04X centre, 03X east.

hr-lm-740393.title: Sign: dark blue street sign, white line
hr-lm-740393.summary: Two dark blue street name signs unique to the capital, always with a white line next to the street name.

hr-lm-740394.title: Landscape: city on the water, ridges north and east
hr-lm-740394.summary: The second biggest city sits by the sea with large mountain ridges to the north and east, many big apartment blocks, one skyscraper, and sometimes an island to the west.

hr-lm-783126.title: Language: Latin letters, Č Š Ž Ć Đ, ulica
hr-lm-783126.summary: Always written in Latin letters. It uses Č, Š, Ž plus Ć and Đ, and the word for street is ulica. Slovene looks similar but lacks Ć and Đ. Lots of lj and nj shows a South Slavic language.

differs.how: Slovene has no Ć or Đ

hr-m4wI.title: Houses: exposed red brick walls
hr-m4wI.summary: Houses sometimes show bare red brick walls, more often inland. Slovenia and Serbia have the same style.

hr-mubM.title: Sign: pedestrian with belt, 5-stripe crossing
hr-mubM.summary: The pedestrian sign shows a person with a belt on a crossing with 5 stripes. Slovenia's pedestrian has no belt.

hr-qQB2.title: Tram: only two cities have them
hr-qQB2.summary: Only the capital and Osijek have trams.

hr-qtTT.title: Guardrail: square B-type
hr-qtTT.summary: Square-profile (B-type) guardrails. Few European countries use this type, so it narrows the guess a lot.

hr-sx0i.title: Google car: side mirrors in the blur
hr-sx0i.summary: In older Gen 3 coverage the car blur often lets the side mirrors show. It happens elsewhere but most often here. A small round yellow sticker on a mirror is unique to this country.

hr-t3Rl.title: Plate: HR sticker on the back
hr-t3Rl.summary: Small stickers with the letters HR (short for Hrvatska) on cars. They were used before EU plates, so they are rarer in newer Gen 4 coverage.

hr-uILw.title: Sign: yellow direction sign with black outline
hr-uILw.summary: Direction signs have a yellow background, a black outline and often a pencil-shaped tip. Slovenia, Serbia, Montenegro and North Macedonia have similar signs.

hr-x9Iz.title: Shops: Karlovačko, Ožujsko, Konzum, Plodine
hr-x9Iz.summary: Ads for Karlovačko and Ožujsko beer are common. Konzum and Plodine are supermarket chains in big cities. Plodine is only here; Konzum also has stores in Bosnia.

differs.how: Konzum also exists in Bosnia, Plodine does not
